title: Keep the nightly price refresh out of everyone else's threads

blocks.text: Every night at two the shop refreshes the price of each SKU from the rate service, a network call of a few hundred milliseconds per SKU. Since the refresh went live, the checkout's address validation, which runs on `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync`, times out for the twenty minutes the refresh takes.

items: `lookUpAll(skus)`: the prices, looked up several SKUs at a time;
`refresh(skus)`: runs `lookUpAll` so that the refresh uses `workers` threads of its own and shares none with the rest of the service; it closes the pool it creates when it's done.

blocks.text: About seven lines in total. The tests use a rate service that answers at once, and check which threads ran the lookups.

cases.says: the refresh returns the rate service's price for every SKU, and an empty map for no SKUs
every lookup runs on a worker of a pool of the refresh's own: not on the calling thread and not in the JVM's common pool
lookups run in parallel inside that pool, so two of them can be in flight at once

origin.section: The Common Pool Is Shared, So Blocking in It Delays Work You Didn't Write

concepts: Parallel streams, CompletableFuture async methods without an executor, and tasks forked outside a pool share the JVM's common pool, so blocking calls there delay unrelated work; a parallel stream also runs on its calling thread.
A parallel stream started from a task of another ForkJoinPool runs in that pool, which keeps blocking work out of the common pool.
